children.translated_text: She who, through <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), leads to peace the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) who desire tranquility,
She who, through <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge), accomplishes the welfare of the world for those who act for the benefit of beings,

children.text: savārkāramidaṃ vadanti munayo viśvaṃ yayā saṃgatā
children.translated_text: She through union with whom the sages declare this entire universe with all its aspects,
To her, who has the <s>Buddha</s> as lord together with the assemblies of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> — homage! //
The path of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects), which the Teacher has taught herein,
The wise should examine it, untouched by others. // Abhs_1.1 //
Keeping in mind the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s>, the practice of <s>Dharma</s> is tenfold;
So that one may easily comprehend it — this is the purpose of the constant endeavor. // Abhs_1.2 //
<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) is set forth through eight topics:
<s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects), <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge), <s>sarvajñatā</s> (all-knowledge), then // Abhs_1.3 //
<s>Sarvākārābhisaṃbodha</s> (complete realization of all aspects), the peak-reached sequential [realization],
<s>Ekakṣaṇābhisaṃbodha</s> (instantaneous realization), and <s>dharmakāya</s> — these are the eight. // Abhs_1.4 //
Generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>), instructions (<s>avavāda</s>), and the fourfold <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (factors of penetration),
The basis of practice, whose nature is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena), // Abhs_1.5 //
The object (<s>ālambana</s>), the intended scope (<s>samuddeśa</s>), the activities of armor-donning (<s>saṃnāha</s>) and setting forth (<s>prasthiti</s>),
And the accumulations (<s>saṃbhāra</s>) together with the definite emergence (<s>niryāṇa</s>) — [these constitute] the <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> of the Sage. // Abhs_1.6 //
The aspects such as obscuration and so forth, and the paths of the disciples (<s>śiṣya</s>) and solitary realizers (<s>khaḍga</s>),
The great benefit, the path of seeing (<s>dṛṅmārga</s>), with its qualities pertaining to this life and the next, // Abhs_1.7 //
Function (<s>kāritra</s>), aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>), praise, eulogy, and commendation,
In dedication (<s>pariṇāma</s>) and rejoicing (<s>anumodana</s>), the two supreme mental applications (<s>manaskāra</s>), // Abhs_1.8 //
Bringing forth (<s>nirhāra</s>), purity (<s>śuddhi</s>), and the ultimate — this is the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāpatha</s>);
It is the knowledge of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Thus <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge) is explained. // Abhs_1.9 //

children.text: prajñayā na bhave sthānaṃ kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), no abiding in <s>bhava</s> (existence); through <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion), no resting in cessation (<s>śama</s>);
Without skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), there is distance; with skillful means, there is nearness. // Abhs_1.10 //
The adverse factors (<s>vipakṣa</s>) and their antidotes (<s>pratipakṣa</s>), the practice (<s>prayoga</s>), and its equality (<s>samatā</s>),
The path of seeing (<s>dṛṅmārga</s>) of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others — thus <s>sarvajñatā</s> (all-knowledge) is explained. // Abhs_1.11 //
Aspects (<s>ākāra</s>) together with their application (<s>prayoga</s>), qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), faults (<s>doṣa</s>), together with their characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>),
The factors conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) and penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), the irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) assembly, // Abhs_1.12 //
Equality (<s>samatā</s>) of existence and cessation, and the unsurpassed purification of the field (<s>kṣetraśuddhi</s>) —
This is the complete realization of all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisaṃbodha</s>), endowed with skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>). // Abhs_1.13 //
Its sign (<s>liṅga</s>), its increase (<s>vivṛddhi</s>), its culmination (<s>nirūḍhi</s>), and the stability of mind (<s>cittasaṃsthiti</s>),
And the fourfold conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) together with its fourfold antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>), // Abhs_1.14 //

children.text: pratyekaṃ darsanākhye ca bhāvanākhye ca vartmani /
children.translated_text: In each of the paths called seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
The uninterrupted concentration (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>), together with the wrong understandings (<s>vipratipatti</s>), // Abhs_1.15 //
The peak <s>abhisamaya</s> (clear realization) is threefold, and the sequential [realization] is tenfold;
<s>Ekakṣaṇābhisaṃbodha</s> (instantaneous realization) is fourfold by its characteristics. // Abhs_1.16 //
<s>Svābhāvika</s> (essential), together with <s>sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment), <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation), and another likewise —
<s>Dharmakāya</s> together with its activity (<s>kāritra</s>) is declared to be fourfold. // Abhs_1.17 //
<s>Cittotpāda</s> (generation of the awakening mind) is the desire for perfect complete awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) for the sake of others;

children.text: samāsavyāsataḥ sā ca yathāsutraṃ sa cocyate // Abhs_1.18 //
children.translated_text: It is described in brief and in detail, in accordance with the <s>sūtras</s>. // Abhs_1.18 //
By [similes of] earth, gold, moon, fire, treasure, jewel-mine, ocean,
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond), mountain, medicine, spiritual friend, wish-fulfilling gem, sun, and song, // Abhs_1.19 //
King, storehouse, great highway, vehicle, fountain, and water,
Joyful sound, river, and cloud — it is of twenty-two kinds. // Abhs_1.20 //
In practice and in the [four] truths, in the three [jewels] — <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Ratna</s> (jewel), and the rest,
In non-attachment, in indefatigability, in the full comprehension of practice, // Abhs_1.21 //
It should be known in the five eyes (<s>cakṣus</s>), in the six <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) qualities,
In the path of seeing (<s>dṛṅmārga</s>) and in [the path] called cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — the instructions (<s>avavāda</s>) are tenfold. // Abhs_1.22 //
Those of dull and sharp faculties, those who have attained through faith and through insight, the <s>kulāṃkula</s> (clan-to-clan) practitioners,
The <s>ekavīcika</s> (one-interval), the <s>antaropapadya</s> (intermediate-born), those going to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> with or without effort, // Abhs_1.23 //
Three who leap, those supreme at the peak of existence, the destroyer of <s>rūparāga</s> (form-realm attachment),
The one who attains peace in this very life, the body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>), and the solitary realizer (<s>khaḍga</s>) — twenty [types]. // Abhs_1.24 //
By virtue of their object (<s>ālambana</s>), aspect (<s>ākāra</s>), causality (<s>hetutva</s>), and full comprehension (<s>saṃparigraha</s>),
Those noble ones who partake of the fourfold conceptual conjunction, each according to their own [capacity], // Abhs_1.25 //
Are distinguished from <s>śrāvakas</s> together with the solitary realizers (<s>khaḍga</s>) — [these are the qualities] of the <s>bodhisattva</s> and Protector;
The distinction of the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat) and other [stages] is in terms of mild, medium, and supreme. // Abhs_1.26 //
The object (<s>ālambana</s>) is impermanence and so forth, based on the [four] truths; its form:
The negation of attachment and the rest, the cause for attaining the three vehicles (<s>yānatraya</s>). // Abhs_1.27 //
The arising and passing away of <s>rūpa</s> (form) and the rest, their abiding and non-abiding, are to be expressed as designations;
The abiding in <s>rūpa</s> and the rest, and their non-selfhood (<s>asvabhāvatā</s>) by virtue of being those [things], // Abhs_1.28 //
The mutual selfhood of those two, their non-fixation in impermanence and the rest,
The emptiness of those [characteristics] with respect to that nature, and the mutual selfhood of these two — // Abhs_1.29 //
The non-grasping of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), the non-examination of their marks,
And the investigation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) through the non-apprehension of everything — // Abhs_1.30 //
The non-selfhood of <s>rūpa</s> (form) and the rest, the selfhood of that non-existence,
Their non-arising, non-departure, purity, and their marklessness, // Abhs_1.31 //
Non-establishment in those marks, non-aspiration, non-conceptualization,
<s>Samādhi</s> (concentration), its function, prediction (<s>vyākṛti</s>), and the inexhaustibility of mind — // Abhs_1.32 //
The mutual selfhood of [each] triad, and the non-conceptualization of <s>samādhi</s> —
Thus the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (factors of penetration) are [distinguished] as mild, medium, and supreme. // Abhs_1.33 //
The duality of the conceptualization of the graspable (<s>grāhya</s>) is by virtue of the thing and its antidote;

children.text: moharāśyādibhedena pratyekaṃ navadhā tu saḥ // Abhs_1.34 //
children.translated_text: Each is ninefold, by the division into delusion-mass and the rest. // Abhs_1.34 //
The grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>) is held to be twofold: based on substance (<s>dravya</s>) and designation (<s>prajñapti</s>),
In the form of an independent self and the rest, and based on the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) and so forth. // Abhs_1.35 //
The non-sinking of mind and so forth, teaching the non-selfhood of [all dharmas],
The complete abandonment of the adversaries, and the full comprehension in every way, // Abhs_1.36 //
Of the sixteenfold <s>dharma</s> of realization, of the antidote and abandonment,

children.text: tayoḥ paryupayogasya prajñāyāḥ kṛpayā saha // Abhs_1.37 //
children.translated_text: Of the employment of those two, of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) together with <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion), // Abhs_1.37 //
Of the uncommon nature with respect to disciples, of the sequential [concern for] others' welfare,
And of the effortless operation of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) — the basis (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) is called <s>gotra</s> (lineage). // Abhs_1.38 //
Since the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) is undivided, a division of <s>gotra</s> (lineage) is not logical;
But due to the division of the qualities to be superimposed (<s>ādheyadharma</s>), its division is proclaimed. // Abhs_1.39 //
The object (<s>ālambana</s>) is all <s>dharmas</s>; they are furthermore wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) and the rest,

children.text: laukikādhigamākhyāścaṃ ye ca lokettarā matāḥ // Abhs_1.40 //
children.translated_text: Mundane (<s>laukika</s>) and those called attainments (<s>adhigama</s>), and those held to be supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>). // Abhs_1.40 //
<s>Dharmas</s> with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) and without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>),

children.text: śiṣyasādhāraṇā dharmā ye cāsādhāranā muneḥ // Abhs_1.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmas</s> common to disciples and those uncommon to the Sage — // Abhs_1.41 //
Supremacy over all beings in the triad of mind, abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>), and realization (<s>adhigama</s>) —
This intended scope (<s>uddeśa</s>) of the Self-arisen Ones (<s>svayaṃbhū</s>) should be known through three greatnesses. // Abhs_1.42 //

children.text: dānādau ṣaḍvidha teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ saṃgraheṇa yā /
children.translated_text: In giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest, the sixfold [perfections], the armor-practice (<s>saṃnāhapratipattiḥ</s>) for each,
In brief, is that which is explained as six sets of six. // Abhs_1.43 //
In the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and formless [attainments], in giving and the rest, on the path, in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest,
In the practice of abandoning apprehension, and in the triple-circle purity (<s>trimaṇḍalaviśuddhi</s>), // Abhs_1.44 //
In the intended scope, in the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), in the path of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects) —
The setting forth (<s>prasthāna</s>) practice should be known as ascending the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). // Abhs_1.45 //
Compassion (<s>dayā</s>), the sixfold group of giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) with <s>vidarśana</s> (insight),

children.text: yuganaddhaśca yo mārga upāye yacca kauśalam // Abhs_1.46 //
children.translated_text: And the path of union (<s>yuganaddha</s>), and whatever is skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>), // Abhs_1.46 //

children.text: jñānaṃ puṇyaṃ ca mārgaśca dhāraṇī bhūmayo daśa /
children.translated_text: <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), merit (<s>puṇya</s>), and the path, <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
And the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) — this should be known as the sequential practice of the accumulations (<s>saṃbhāra</s>). // Abhs_1.47 //
The first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) is attained through tenfold preparatory practice (<s>parikarman</s>):
Intention (<s>āśaya</s>), being of beneficial nature, equanimity (<s>samacittatā</s>) toward beings, // Abhs_1.48 //
Renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>), attendance upon spiritual friends (<s>mitra</s>), seeking the <s>saddharma</s> (true Dharma) as object,
Constant mental inclination toward renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>), aspiration toward the body of the <s>Buddha</s>, // Abhs_1.49 //
Teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, truthfulness — the tenth is said to be speech;
And the preparatory practice of these should be known through the non-apprehension of their own nature. // Abhs_1.50 //

children.text: śīlaṃ kṛtajñatā kṣāntiḥ pramodyaṃ mahatī kṛpā /
children.translated_text: Moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), gratitude (<s>kṛtajñatā</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), joy (<s>pramodya</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākṛpā</s>),
Reverence (<s>gaurava</s>), attendance upon the teacher (<s>guruśuśrūṣā</s>), diligence (<s>vīrya</s>) — the eighth is in giving and the rest. // Abhs_1.51 //

children.text: atṛptatā śrute dānaṃ dharmasya ca nirāmiṣam /
children.translated_text: Insatiability in learning, giving of the <s>Dharma</s> without material [expectation],
Purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), unweariness in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), // Abhs_1.52 //
Moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>apatrāpya</s>) — this is fivefold in nature as mindfulness (<s>manana</s>);
Forest-dwelling, having few desires, contentment, observing the <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) and austerity practices, // Abhs_1.53 //
Non-abandonment of the training (<s>śikṣā</s>), disgust toward sense pleasures (<s>kāma</s>),
Disenchantment, renunciation of all possessions, non-sinking mind, and non-attachment, // Abhs_1.54 //
Socializing, household attachment, maintaining a position that leads to socializing,
Self-exaltation and contempt for others, the ten unwholesome paths of action (<s>karmamārga</s>) — // Abhs_1.55 //
Abandoning pride, arrogance, wrong views, doubt, and tolerance of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

children.text: vivarjayan samāpneti daśaitān pañcamīṃ bhuvam // Abhs_1.56 //
children.translated_text: one attains these ten [qualities] and the fifth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). // Abhs_1.56 //
Through the fulfillment of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣamā</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
one who abandons the minds that desire the <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) and <s>khaḍga</s> (solitary rhinoceros) [paths], and [minds of] fear, // Abhs_1.57 //
who when asked is not withdrawn, and even in giving away everything is not disheartened,

children.text: kṛśo 'pi nārthināṃ kṣeptā ṣaṣṭhīṃ bhūmiṃ samaśrute // Abhs_1.58 //
children.translated_text: who though impoverished does not turn away supplicants — such a one attains the sixth <s>bhūmi</s>. // Abhs_1.58 //
Grasping at self and beings, [views of] <s>jīva</s> (life-soul) and <s>pudgala</s> (person), eternalism and annihilationism,
signs and causes regarding the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), // Abhs_1.59 //
abiding in the three realms, attachment, a sunken mind,
clinging to views regarding the Three Jewels and <s>śīla</s> (morality), // Abhs_1.60 //
disputing about <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), and opposing it — these twenty

children.text: kalaṅkā yasya vicChinnāḥ saptamīmetyasau bhuvam // Abhs_1.61 //
children.translated_text: blemishes, when severed, [enable] one to attain the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>. // Abhs_1.61 //
Knowledge of the three gates of liberation, purity of the three spheres,
compassionate non-attachment, knowledge of the equality and single method of <s>dharmas</s>, // Abhs_1.62 //
knowledge and patience regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>, comprehending <s>dharmas</s> as one,
uprooting of conceptual proliferation, abandoning perception, views, and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), // Abhs_1.63 //

children.text: śamathasya ca nidhyaptiḥ kauśalaṃ ca vidarśane /
children.translated_text: attainment of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), and skill in <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight),

children.text: cittasya dāntatā jñānaṃ sarvatrāpratighāti ca // Abhs_1.64 //
children.translated_text: taming of the mind, knowledge that is unobstructed everywhere, // Abhs_1.64 //
non-abiding in attachment, going to other realms as one wishes, equally

children.text: sarvatra svātmabhāvasya darśanaṃ ceti viṃśatiḥ // Abhs_1.65 //
children.translated_text: seeing one's own nature everywhere — these are the twenty [qualities of the eighth <s>bhūmi</s>]. // Abhs_1.65 //
Knowledge of the minds of all beings, sport with <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), [establishing] the auspicious
accomplishment of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), and attending and examining the <s>Buddhas</s>, // Abhs_1.66 //
knowledge of the faculties, purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field, abiding as if in an illusion,
and intentionally taking birth in existence — this eightfold <s>karma</s> (activity) is proclaimed. // Abhs_1.67 //
Infinite <s>praṇidhānas</s> (aspirations), knowledge of the speech of gods and others,
eloquence [flowing] like a river, and the supreme entry into the womb, // Abhs_1.68 //
excellence of family and birth, of lineage,
of retinue, of birth, of renunciation, of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, and of the fulfillment of qualities — // Abhs_1.69 //
having transcended the nine <s>bhūmis</s>, one is established on the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (buddha-stage).

children.text: yena jñānena sā jñeyā daśamī bodhisattvabhūḥ // Abhs_1.70 //
children.translated_text: By which knowledge that tenth <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>bhūmi</s> is to be known. // Abhs_1.70 //
The <s>pratipakṣa</s> (antidote) should be known as eightfold, in the paths of seeing and cultivation,
for the pacification of the eight types of conceptual elaboration of the apprehended and the apprehender. // Abhs_1.71 //
Regarding the summary, equality, the welfare of beings, and the abandonment of effort,

children.text: atyantāya ca niryāṇaṃ niryāṇaṃ prāptilakṣaṇam // Abhs_1.72 //
children.translated_text: and regarding the ultimate — the <s>niryāṇa</s> (emergence) has the characteristic of attainment. // Abhs_1.72 //
And regarding <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), the <s>niryāṇa</s> pertains to the path.
The practice of <s>niryāṇa</s> should be known as eightfold in nature. // Abhs_1.73 //

body.translated_text: // End of the first chapter on <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) in the <s>Abhisamayālaṃkāra</s>, a treatise of instruction on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

children.translated_text: Dimming by its radiance, suitability for the gods,

children.text: viṣayo niyato vyāptiḥ svabhāvastasya karma ca // Abhs_2.1 //
children.translated_text: a definite object, pervasion, its nature, and its action — // Abhs_2.1 //
through the non-apprehension of the aspects of the four noble truths,
this path of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) should be known in the method of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths). // Abhs_2.2 //
From the emptiness of form and other <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), from the non-differentiation of types of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: uṣmāṇaḥ anupalambhena teṣāṃ murdhagataṃ matam // Abhs_2.3 //
children.translated_text: through non-apprehension [this constitutes] <s>uṣmagata</s> (heat); their culmination is considered <s>mūrdhagata</s> (summit). // Abhs_2.3 //
<s>Kṣāntis</s> (acceptances) are through the negation of abiding in permanence and such [views] regarding those;
beginning from the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, through teaching the extent and non-abiding, // Abhs_2.4 //
<s>Agradharmagata</s> (supreme dharma) is proclaimed on the path of the noble <s>śrāvakas</s>.
For what reason? Because the <s>Buddha</s>, having awakened, saw that <s>dharmas</s> are unequal. // Abhs_2.5 //
The futility of instructing others, due to self-awakening, of the self-born ones,
and the profundity of their knowledge — this is declared as the [path of the] <s>khaḍgas</s> (solitary realizers). // Abhs_2.6 //

children.text: śuśrūṣā yasya yasyārthe yatra yatra yathā yathā /
children.translated_text: The desire to hear, for whatever purpose, wherever, and in whatever manner,

children.text: sa so 'rthaḥ khyātyaśabdo 'pi tasya tasya tathā tathā // Abhs_2.7 //
children.translated_text: that purpose becomes known, even without words, to each one accordingly. // Abhs_2.7 //
Through the abandonment of conceptualizing apprehended objects, the non-abandonment of the apprehender,
and from the basis — the summary of the <s>khaḍga</s>-path should be understood. // Abhs_2.8 //
Having the form of indicating <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) without contradicting conventional designation,
<s>uṣmagata</s> (heat) and <s>mūrdhagata</s> (summit) are characterized by non-abandonment of form and so forth. // Abhs_2.9 //
Through internal emptiness and so forth, by not grasping form and the rest,
<s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance); through aspects such as non-arising of form and the rest, <s>agradharmatā</s> (supreme dharma). // Abhs_2.10 //
Through the fourfold moments of <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), regarding each truth,
the path of seeing in <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) — this is said to have its benefits. // Abhs_2.11 //
From the absence of the relation of support and supported between <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and <s>buddhas</s>,
non-cognition by way of synonyms, greatness, and immeasurability, // Abhs_2.12 //
absence of limits in measure, ascertainment of form and so forth,
and while abiding in that, blessings for <s>buddhahood</s> and going beyond, and so forth — // Abhs_2.13 //
<s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and so forth, attainment of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), embracing <s>buddhahood</s>,
the cure of all diseases of all purification, // Abhs_2.14 //
the pacification of grasping at <s>nirvāṇa</s>, protection from <s>Buddhas</s> and so forth,
beginning from non-killing of living beings, in the method of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) — // Abhs_2.15 //
while oneself abiding, establishing beings, the <s>pariṇāmana</s> (dedication)
of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest toward <s>saṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening) — these are the aspects of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths). // Abhs_2.16 //
The taming called 'universal,' the conquest of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) everywhere,
irresistibility comparable [to nothing], <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) as the basis of worship — // Abhs_2.17 //
<s>adhimukti</s> (aspiration) should be known as threefold: for one's own benefit, for one's own and others' benefit,
and for others' benefit — and each of these is further considered threefold. // Abhs_2.18 //
Mild, middling, and intense, with subdivisions of mild-mild and so forth,
each again being threefold — thus it is considered twenty-sevenfold. // Abhs_2.19 //

children.text: stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca prajñāparamitāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Praise, eulogy, and commendation toward <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> —
the degrees of <s>adhimokṣa</s> (aspiration) are considered as three sets of nine. // Abhs_2.20 //
The distinction is <s>pariṇāma</s> (dedication), and its supreme function
has the form of non-apprehension and the characteristic of non-error. // Abhs_2.21 //
It is isolated, has the nature of the flood of <s>Buddha</s>'s merit, is within the scope of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness),
is endowed with skillful means, is signless, and is approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. // Abhs_2.22 //
Not entered into the three realms — the other <s>pariṇāma</s> (dedication) is threefold:
mild, middling, and intense, having the nature of a great arising of merit. // Abhs_2.23 //
Through skillful means and non-apprehension, the <s>anumodanā</s> (rejoicing) in roots of virtue
is established here through rejoicing, mental attention, and cultivation. // Abhs_2.24 //
Its nature, its supreme quality, the non-fabrication of everything,
the dedication of <s>dharmas</s> through non-apprehension, and its great significance — // Abhs_2.25 //
service to the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest, and whatever skill in means,
these are the causes of <s>adhimokṣa</s> (aspiration); the causes of decline in <s>Dharma</s> [are as follows]: // Abhs_2.26 //
influence of <s>Māra</s>, non-aspiration toward the profound <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality),
clinging to <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the rest, and association with evil friends. // Abhs_2.27 //
The purity of the result and the purity of form and so forth — of those two,
since they are undifferentiated and unbroken, this purity is proclaimed. // Abhs_2.28 //
Of the <s>kleśa</s> (affliction), <s>jñeya</s> (cognitive), and three-path [obscurations] of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), <s>khaḍgas</s> (solitary realizers), and <s>Buddha</s>'s heirs,
purity is through abandonment; but the <s>Buddha</s>'s [purity] is ultimate in every way. // Abhs_2.29 //
The path beginning with mild-mild, purity in the nine <s>bhūmis</s>,
as the antidote to defilements beginning with the most intense of the most intense — // Abhs_2.30 //
being the antidote to the three realms, equality of the measurable and immeasurable
of the path — this is considered through elimination. // Abhs_2.31 //

body.translated_text: // End of the second chapter on <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) in the <s>Abhisamayālaṃkāra</s>, a treatise of instruction on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

children.text: nāpare na pare tīre nāntarāle tathoḥ sthitā /
children.translated_text: Not on this shore, not on the far shore, nor standing in between,
from the knowledge of the equality of the three times, she is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. // Abhs_3.1 //
Without skillful means she is far away, due to signs and apprehension;
through skill in means, her proper nearness is proclaimed. // Abhs_3.2 //
Regarding the emptiness of form and other <s>skandhas</s>, regarding <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to the three times,
regarding <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest and the factors of awakening — the perception of practice is the adverse factor. // Abhs_3.3 //
Non-ego-making regarding <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest, engaging others in that,
the negation of the extreme of attachment — this subtle attachment is toward the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) and so forth. // Abhs_3.4 //
Its profundity is by its very nature, from the isolation of the way of <s>dharmas</s>;
knowledge of a single nature, the abandonment of attachment to <s>dharmas</s>. // Abhs_3.5 //
Through the negation of views and so forth, its difficult-to-comprehend nature is proclaimed;
from its being unknowable through form and the rest, its inconceivability is maintained. // Abhs_3.6 //

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā yathokto vai jñeyaḥ sarvajñatānaye /
children.translated_text: Having done thus, as has been stated, in the method of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all),
this classification of adverse factors and antidotes is to be known as exhaustive. // Abhs_3.7 //
Regarding form and so on, their impermanence and so on, their not being full or being full,
and the non-attachment to them in practice: the application is through negation. // Abhs 3.8 //

children.text: avikāro na kartā ca prayogo duṣkarastridhā /
children.translated_text: Unchangeable, not an agent, the application is threefold as difficult to perform;
it is not barren because of the attainment of fruits as they are to be, and it is as desired. // Abhs 3.9 //
And that which does not depend on another is sevenfold, making known through cognition;

children.text: caturdhā mananā tasya rūpādau samatā matā // Abhs_3.10 //
children.translated_text: its contemplation is fourfold; equanimity regarding form and so on is taught. // Abhs 3.10 //
Consisting of the moments of <s>dharma-jñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas), <s>anvaya-jñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge), <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
this is the path of seeing regarding the truth of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) and so on, in the method of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). // Abhs 3.11 //
Form is neither permanent nor impermanent; it transcends extremes and is pure;
it is unborn, unceased, and so on; it is like space, free from defilement. // Abhs 3.12 //
Liberated from grasping, inexpressible by its very nature,

children.text: pravyāhāreṇa nāsyārthaḥ pareṣu prāpyate yataḥ // Abhs_3.13 //
children.translated_text: because through verbal expression its true meaning is not conveyed to others. // Abhs 3.13 //
Not producing apprehension, utterly pure, free from the arising of affliction,
the impossibility of falling into lower realms and of conceptual elaboration — toward the direct realization of the fruit. // Abhs 3.14 //
Non-association with causes, with respect to the object, to the indication, to both,
and the non-arising of knowledge — these are the moments of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). // Abhs 3.15 //

children.text: iti seyaṃ punaḥ seyaṃ seyaṃ khalu punastridhā /
children.translated_text: 'Thus this again,' 'this indeed again' — threefold,
the completion of the three topics is thus illuminated. // Abhs 3.16 //

body.translated_text: // In the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instruction on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the third chapter on <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) //

children.translated_text: The aspects of the modes of knowledge of things are the defining characteristic;

children.text: sarvajñatānāṃ traividyāt trividhā eva te matāḥ // Abhs_4.1 //
children.translated_text: due to the threefold nature of the three kinds of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), they are considered to be of three types. // Abhs 4.1 //
Beginning from the aspect of non-existence up to the aspect of immovability,

children.text: catvāraḥ pratisatyaṃ te mārge pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ // Abhs_4.2 //
children.translated_text: there are four for each truth; on the path, fifteen are taught. // Abhs 4.2 //

children.text: hetau mārge ca duḥkhe ca nirodhe ca yathākramam /
children.translated_text: Regarding the cause, the path, <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), respectively,

children.text: aṣṭau te sapta pañceti ṣoḍaśeti ca kīrtitāḥ // Abhs_4.3 //
children.translated_text: they are declared as eight, seven, five, and sixteen. // Abhs 4.3 //
Beginning from the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) and ending with the aspects of Buddhahood,

children.text: śiṣyāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ buddhānāṃ ca yathākramam // Abhs_4.4 //
children.translated_text: for <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Buddhas</s>, respectively, // Abhs 4.4 //
they are considered to be thirty-seven, thirty-four, and thirty-nine,
according to the threefold division of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), in conformity with the truth of the path. // Abhs 4.5 //
Those who have completed their training under <s>Buddhas</s>, who have planted roots of merit in their presence,
who are supported by virtuous spiritual friends — they are the vessels for hearing this teaching. // Abhs 4.6 //
Through attending upon <s>Buddhas</s>, asking questions, practicing generosity, morality, and so on,
the capacity for memorization, retention, and so on is considered by the wise. // Abhs 4.7 //
Due to the instability of form and so on, due to the prohibition of attachment to them,
due to the profundity of their <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and due to their being difficult to fathom, // Abhs 4.8 //
due to their not being a valid means of knowledge, due to awakening with difficulty and over a long time,
regarding prediction and the state of non-retrogression, and in the stages of departure with and without remainder, // Abhs 4.9 //
and when <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is near, swiftly, for the benefit of others, without increase or decrease,
and in the non-seeing of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, and in the non-seeing of form as inconceivable and so on, // Abhs 4.10 //
non-conceptual regarding form and so on, their causes, and their existence;

children.text: phalaratnapradātā ca śuddhakaḥ sāvadhiśca saḥ // Abhs_4.11 //
children.translated_text: a bestower of the jewel of the fruit, a purifier, and one who has a limit. // Abhs 4.11 //
The diminishment of <s>Māras'</s> power and so forth — fourteen kinds of qualities;
and six faults are to be understood, together with four groups of ten. // Abhs 4.12 //

children.text: lakṣyate yena tajjñeyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: That by which something is characterized should be known as the characteristic, and it is threefold:

children.text: jñānaṃ viśeṣaḥ kāritraṃ svabhāvo yaśca lakṣyate // Abhs_4.13 //
children.translated_text: knowledge, distinction, function, and the nature that is characterized. // Abhs 4.13 //
Regarding the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and regarding the world as not coming to an end,
regarding the mental conduct of beings, regarding their summary, and regarding external manifestation, // Abhs 4.14 //
regarding the aspect of inexhaustibility, regarding those with passion and so on when elaborated,
regarding the great, the immeasurable, and regarding consciousness as without visible indication, // Abhs 4.15 //
and regarding the knowledge of the invisible mind — this is designated as the extraction and so on;
furthermore, through the aspect of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), knowledge of them beyond this. // Abhs 4.16 //
Regarding <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and the awakening of the Sage — this narration is called supreme;
this is the summary of the characteristic of knowledge in the chapter on <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). // Abhs 4.17 //
Regarding emptiness, signlessness, and the absence of aspiration,
regarding non-arising, cessation, and so on, and the unshakeability of the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, // Abhs 4.18 //
regarding non-conditioning and non-conceptualization, and regarding the differentiation and characteristiclessness —
this is considered the characteristic of knowledge in the chapter on <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the path). // Abhs 4.19 //
Relying on one's own <s>dharmas</s>, in the practice of them, in their veneration,
in their weightiness, in their honoring, and in the worship and non-fabrication of them, // Abhs 4.20 //
knowledge that operates everywhere, that reveals what is unseen,
that indicates the aspect of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of the world, that makes known, and that is unobstructed, // Abhs 4.21 //
that perceives the inconceivable and the quiescent, and that suppresses the designations of the world —
this is declared to be the characteristic of knowledge in the method of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). // Abhs 4.22 //
Through the distinction of inconceivability and so on, with distinguished objects of truth,
the distinguishing characteristic is taught through six and ten moments. // Abhs 4.23 //
Inconceivability, incomparability, surpassing what is to be measured and what is countable,
inclusion of all <s>āryas</s> (noble ones), knowledge cognizable by the wise, and uncommon knowledge, // Abhs 4.24 //
swift knowledge, neither deficiency nor excess, attainment and arising,

children.text: ālambanaṃ ca sādhāraṃ sākalyaṃ saṃparigrahaḥ // Abhs_4.25 //
children.translated_text: common object of support, completeness, and full comprehension, // Abhs 4.25 //
and non-relishing — the distinction is to be known as sixteenfold.
The distinguishing paths are those by which this path is distinguished from other paths. // Abhs 4.26 //

children.text: hitaṃ sukhaṃ ca trāṇaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ layanaṃ nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: Benefit, happiness, protection, refuge, and resting place for beings,

children.text: parāyaṇaṃ ca dvīpaṃ ca pariṇāyakasaṃjñakam // Abhs_4.27 //
children.translated_text: ultimate resort, island, and that which is called the guide, // Abhs 4.27 //
effortless, with the three vehicles, having the nature of the direct realization of the fruit,
and final — this is the characteristic of function. // Abhs 4.28 //
The discernment of the marks, signs, and causes of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
of the opponent and its antidote, the difficult one, the definite; the exposition is through non-apprehension. // Abhs 4.29 //
The negation of clinging, and that which is called the object of support,
non-aversion, non-obstruction, and that which has no basis, no destination, no birth. // Abhs 4.30 //
Non-apprehension of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and nature — sixteenfold;

children.text: lakṣmeva lakṣyate ceticaturthaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ matam // Abhs_4.31 //
children.translated_text: it is characterized like a mark — this is considered the fourth characteristic. // Abhs 4.31 //
Skill in the arising of signless giving and so on —
in this comprehension of all aspects, the share conducive to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is taught. // Abhs 4.32 //
<s>Śraddhā</s> (faith) with <s>Buddhas</s> and so on as its object, <s>vīrya</s> (effort) directed toward generosity and so on,
<s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) as the perfection of intention, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) as non-conceptualization, // Abhs 4.33 //
and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> in all their aspects — thus fivefold.
Through sharp faculties, awakening is easy; through dull ones, it is considered difficult. // Abhs 4.34 //
All sentient beings are the object of support; herein, the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat) stage is possible;
the aspect beginning with equanimity of mind toward them is taught as tenfold. // Abhs 4.35 //
Of one who has turned away from evil and who abides in generosity and so on,
the engagement of others in both of these, and speaking in praise of them, in accordance. // Abhs 4.36 //
The <s>mūrdhagata</s> (summit stage): support of self and others, knowledge of truth, and also forbearance;
likewise, the <s>agradharmas</s> (supreme dharmas stage) is to be known through the ripening of beings and so on. // Abhs 4.37 //
Beginning from the <s>nirvedhabhāgīyas</s> (factors conducive to penetration), on the paths of seeing and cultivation,

children.text: ye bodhisattvā vartante so 'trāvaivartiko gaṇaḥ // Abhs_4.38 //
children.translated_text: those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who abide — they are the irreversible assembly here. // Abhs 4.38 //
Through signs such as turning away from form and so on, stated as twenty,
this is the characteristic of irreversibility of one who abides in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> stage. // Abhs 4.39 //
Turning away from form and so on, the destruction of doubt and the momentary <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
of oneself abiding in virtue, and engaging others in the same, // Abhs 4.40 //
being a support for others, generosity and so on, non-craving even in profound matters,
friendliness, non-association with body and so on, and through the fivefold obscuration, // Abhs 4.41 //
the abandonment of all latent tendencies, mindfulness and clear comprehension, purity,
and the non-arising of worms in robes, the body, and so on, // Abhs 4.42 //
non-crookedness of mind, taking up the <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) practices, freedom from miserliness and so on,
going in accordance with the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, seeking even the hells for the benefit of the world, // Abhs 4.43 //
not being led by others, recognizing <s>Māra</s> who teaches another path
as <s>Māra</s>, and conduct that is approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. // Abhs 4.44 //
One who abides in the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat), <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit), <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance), and <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharmas) stages,
through these twenty signs, does not turn back from <s>saṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening). // Abhs 4.45 //

children.text: kṣāntijñānakṣaṇaḥ ṣaṭ ca pañca pañca ca dṛkpathe /
children.translated_text: Six moments of <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), and five and five on the path of seeing —
this is to be known as the characteristic of irreversibility of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. // Abhs 4.46 //
The turning away from the designation of form and so on, firmness of mind regarding the lesser
vehicles, turning away from them, and the exhaustion of the factors of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and so on, // Abhs 4.47 //
lightness of body and mind, the attitude toward sense-pleasure as merely a means,
perpetual chastity, and purity of livelihood, // Abhs 4.48 //
regarding the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so on as obstacles, in the collection together with the sense-faculties and so on,

children.text: samare matsarādau ca neti yogānuyogayoḥ // Abhs_4.49 //
children.translated_text: and in [freedom from] envy and the like — 'it is not so' in the [context of] application and counter-application. // Abhs 4.49 //
The prohibition of [wrong] abiding, and the non-apprehension of the subtle [nature of] <s>dharmas</s>;
certainty in one's own stage, and establishment in the three stages — // Abhs 4.50 //
and the sacrifice of life for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s> — these are the sixteen moments.
These are the signs of irreversibility (<s>avaivartika</s>) of the wise one stationed on the path of seeing (<s>dṛṅmārga</s>). // Abhs 4.51 //
The cultivation path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) is profound; its profundity [consists in] emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and the like.
Freedom from the extremes of superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>) — that is profundity. // Abhs 4.52 //
Reflection, weighing, and meditative absorption — [these constitute] the repeated path of cultivation,

children.text: nirvedhāṅgeṣu dṛṅmārge bhāvanāmārga eva ca // Abhs_4.53 //
children.translated_text: in the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), on the path of seeing, and on the path of cultivation itself. // Abhs 4.53 //
That [path] is taught as having the character of continuity, and is ninefold in its modes:
through the divisions of weak, medium, and strong — and again [each of those subdivided into] weak and so forth. // Abhs 4.54 //
Statements about 'innumerable' and the like are not tenable in the ultimate sense.
They are outflows of compassion, accepted by the Sage conventionally (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). // Abhs 4.55 //
Decrease and increase are not applicable to a thing that is beyond description.

children.text: bhāvanākhyena kiṃ hinaṃ vartmanā kimudāgatam // Abhs_4.56 //
children.translated_text: What is diminished by the path called 'cultivation'? What has been attained? // Abhs 4.56 //
Just as awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) [is], so too is that [path] the accomplisher of the desired aim.

children.text: tathatālakṣaṇā bodhiḥ so 'pi tallakṣaṇo mataḥ // Abhs_4.57 //
children.translated_text: Awakening has the characteristic of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); that [path] too is regarded as having that characteristic. // Abhs 4.57 //

children.text: pūrveṇa bodhirno yuktā manasā paścimena vā /
children.translated_text: Awakening is not [accomplished] by the prior mind or by the subsequent [mind].
Through the analogy of a lamp, the profundity of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) is eightfold. // Abhs 4.58 //

children.text: utpāde ca nirodhe ca tathatāyāṃ gabhīratā /
children.translated_text: There is profundity in arising and in cessation, in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),

children.text: jñeye dāne ca caryāyāmadvayopāyakauśale ca // Abhs_4.59 //
children.translated_text: in the knowable, in giving, in conduct, and in skill in non-dual means. // Abhs 4.59 //
Because of the dream-like nature of <s>dharmas</s>, there is no conceptualization of either existence or peace.
The refutations of objections concerning the non-existence of <s>karma</s> and the like are as stated. // Abhs 4.60 //
The purification of the world of beings — through the offering of that purification,
and likewise the purification of the receptacle-world — is the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field. // Abhs 4.61 //
Its domain, its practice, the transcending of hostile [factors],
non-abiding, [being effective] as far as needed, and having uncommon characteristics — // Abhs 4.62 //
unattached, non-apprehending, free from signs (<s>nimitta</s>) and aspirations (<s>praṇidhi</s>),
having those marks, and immeasurable — [these are] the tenfold skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>). // Abhs 4.63 //

body.translated_text:
// In the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the teaching-treatise on the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>),
the fourth chapter on the complete awakening in all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisaṃbodha</s>) //

children.translated_text: Even within a dream, perceiving all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like, and the like —

children.text: murdhaprāptasya yogasya liṅgaṃ dvādaśadhā matam // Abhs_5.1 //
children.translated_text: this is regarded as the twelvefold sign of the yoga that has attained the summit (<s>mūrdhaprāpta</s>). // Abhs 5.1 //
Making manifold comparisons with the beings born on <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>, wholesome [deeds], and the like —

children.text: upamāṃ bahudhā kṛtvā vivṛddhiḥ ṣoḍaśātmikā // Abhs_5.2 //
children.translated_text: the increase [of merit] is sixteenfold. // Abhs 5.2 //
The supreme fulfillment of the <s>dharmas</s> of the three types of omniscience,
without abandoning the welfare of beings — is called the firmly established [stage] (<s>nirūḍhi</s>). // Abhs 5.3 //
Comparable to [the beings of] the four continents, a thousand, two thousand, and three thousand [world-systems] —
the <s>samādhi</s> is proclaimed, through the abundance of merit. // Abhs 5.4 //

children.text: pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca pratyekaṃ tau navātmakau /
children.translated_text: In the aspects of engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>), [there are] individually ninefold
conceptualizations (<s>vikalpas</s>) regarding the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) — to be known as having the nature of non-accordance with reality. // Abhs 5.5 //
The conceptualizations of substance, designation, existent, and being are regarded as [conceptualizations of] the apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>).
Through the distinction of ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) and noble ones (<s>ārya</s>), [there are] individually ninefold [of each]. // Abhs 5.6 //

children.text: grāhyau cenna tathā sto 'rthau kasya tau grāhakau matau /
children.translated_text: If the apprehended [objects] are not so [i.e., do not exist as apprehended], then whose apprehenders are those [conceptualizations] regarded [to be]?
Thus, by [the negation of] the nature of apprehender, the characteristic of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) of those [is established]. // Abhs 5.7 //
This [conceptualization operates] with regard to intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), practice, and accomplishment;
with regard to the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>) and non-error of knowledge; and with regard to antidote and opponent. // Abhs 5.8 //
With regard to oneself, attainment, the agent, its function, action, and fruit —
the conceptualization based on the aspect of engagement (<s>pravṛttipakṣa</s>) is regarded as ninefold. // Abhs 5.9 //
From falling into [the extremes of] existence and peace; in the deficiency of attainment;
in the absence of full comprehension; in the imperfection of what has been attained on the path; // Abhs 5.10 //
in dependence on others' guidance; in the reversal of what has been indicated;
in partiality; in diversity; and in confusion of station and departure — // Abhs 5.11 //
and in going backward — this is the ninefold conceptualization
based on the aspect of cessation (<s>nivṛttipakṣa</s>), born of the minds of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others. // Abhs 5.12 //
The first [type of] apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) should be known in the grasping and liberating [of beings],
in mental activity regarding the elements (<s>dhātus</s>), and in the conjunction of the three [vehicles]; // Abhs 5.13 //
in station, in clinging, in the designation of <s>dharma</s>-objects,

children.text: saktau ca pratipakṣe ca yathecChaṃ ca gatikṣatau // Abhs_5.14 //
children.translated_text: in attachment, in the antidote, and in the destruction of [the path] at will; // Abhs 5.14 //
in non-deliverance according to the indication; in the determination of path and non-path;
in cessation and in arising; in the conjunction and disjunction with reality; // Abhs 5.15 //
in station, in the destruction of the spiritual lineage, in the absence of aspiration and cause;
and in the apprehension by adversaries — this is the other apprehender-conceptualization. // Abhs 5.16 //
The demonstrations of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) to these [beings], and the gift of its cause;
the immediate cause of attaining that — characterized by the abundance of merit; // Abhs 5.17 //
In the knowledge of the exhaustion and non-arising of the defilements, awakening is said [to consist].
Because of the non-existence of exhaustion and non-arising — those are indeed the knowable, in their respective order. // Abhs 5.18 //
Since the [dharma]-nature has not ceased, by the path called 'seeing,'
has the totality of conceptualizations been exhausted, or has it attained non-arising? // Abhs 5.19 //

children.text: sattā ca nāma dharmāṇāṃ jñeye cāvaraṇakṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The existence of <s>dharmas</s> [as such], and the exhaustion of obstructions regarding the knowable —

children.text: kathyate yatparaiḥ śāsturatra vismīyate mayā // Abhs_5.20 //
children.translated_text: what others teach about this — I marvel at it here, [says] the Master. // Abhs 5.20 //
There is nothing whatsoever to be removed from this, and nothing whatsoever to be added.

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ bhūtadarśī vimucyate // Abhs_5.21 //
children.translated_text: Reality should be seen as it truly is — the seer of reality is liberated. // Abhs 5.21 //

children.text: ekaikasyaiva dānādau teṣāṃ yaḥ saṃgraho mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mutual inclusion of each [perfection] — generosity and the rest — within each,
is [understood as] the instantaneous [realization], included in patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), here on the path of seeing. // Abhs 5.22 //
Having entered that <s>samādhi</s>, then [performing] the lion's sport (<s>siṃhavijṛmbhita</s>),
in forward and reverse order, one examines dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). // Abhs 5.23 //
Having determined the desire-realm [consciousness] and the unconcentrated consciousness,
the attainments (<s>samāpattis</s>) including cessation — having entered and emerged, are twofold in nine [modes]. // Abhs 5.24 //
By skipping over one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and eight [stages],
the 'leaping' attainment (<s>avaskandasamāpatti</s>) — up to cessation — is [established as] incomparable. // Abhs 5.25 //
In brief and in detail, by the <s>Buddhas</s>, in protection and in non-grasping,
in the three times, in the absence of qualities, and in the threefold path of excellence — // Abhs 5.26 //
this is the single conceptualization regarding the apprehended, having practice, aspect, and domain.
The second is regarded as having the activity of mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) as its domain. // Abhs 5.27 //
The non-arising of mind, the mental engagement at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>),
the mental engagements of the lesser vehicle, and the non-engagement with full awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>); // Abhs 5.28 //
regarding cultivation and non-cultivation, and also the reverse of those —
the conceptualization on the path of cultivation should be known as [regarding things] not in accordance with reality. // Abhs 5.29 //
The first apprehender should be known as having the domain of the designation of beings;
as attachment and discrimination with respect to the non-emptiness of <s>dharma</s>-designation. // Abhs 5.30 //

children.text: kṛtena vastuno yānatritaye ca sa kīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is proclaimed with respect to what has been done, to objects, and to the three vehicles;

children.text: dakṣiṇāyā aśuddhau ca caryāyāśca vikopane // Abhs_5.31 //
children.translated_text: and in the impurity of the gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), and in the disturbance of practice. // Abhs 5.31 //
Having the domain of the designation of beings and its causes — the other [apprehender] is ninefold.
Being awakened on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), the opponent [is overcome] through the destruction of that. // Abhs 5.32 //
In the threefold covering of the three types of omniscience, each respectively;
on the path of peace, in the conjunction and disjunction with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and the like; // Abhs 5.33 //
in the inequality regarding suffering and the rest; even in the nature of the afflictions;

children.text: dvayābhāve ca saṃmohe vikalpaḥ paścimo mataḥ // Abhs_5.34 //
children.translated_text: in the absence of duality; and in confusion — the last conceptualization is regarded [thus]. // Abhs 5.34 //
Upon the exhaustion of these [conceptualizations], like breathing again after long [submersion],
the perfections of qualities that accomplish the happiness of the entire world in all aspects [arise]. // Abhs 5.35 //
All [perfections], with total convergence, bearing the fruit of all desires,
attend upon that great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), as rivers [flow into] the great ocean. // Abhs 5.36 //
Establishing the beings of the three-thousand[-fold world system] in the attainment of disciples and solitary [awakeners],

children.text: bodhisattvasya ca nyāmo pratiṣṭāpya śubhopamāḥ // Abhs_5.37 //
children.translated_text: and of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — having established [them, setting up] comparisons of wholesome [merit]; // Abhs 5.37 //
through the abundance of merit thus created, the immediate [cause] for the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s> —

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiḥ sa sarvākārajñatā ca tat // Abhs_5.38 //
children.translated_text: that is the <s>ānantaryasamādhi</s> (concentration without interval), and that [leads to] the omniscience of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). // Abhs 5.38 //
Its object-support is the absence [of object-support]; and mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is regarded as its sovereign.
Its aspect is pacification — of those who engage in talk, counter-talk, and discourse. // Abhs 5.39 //
In the object-support and its arising; in the ascertainment of its intrinsic nature;
in the knowledge of the omniscience of all aspects; in the ultimate and in the conventional; // Abhs 5.40 //

children.text: prayoge triṣu ratneṣu sopāye samaye muneḥ /
children.translated_text: in practice, in the Three Jewels, and in means; in the teaching of the Sage;
in inversion, on the right path, and with respect to antidote and opponent; // Abhs 5.41 //
in characteristics and in cultivation — these are regarded as the wrong conceptions (<s>vipratipattis</s>).

children.text: sarvākārajñatādhārā ṣoḍhā daśa ca cādinām // Abhs_5.42 //
children.translated_text: Based on the omniscience of all aspects — sixteenfold, and [also] ten, and so on of the first. // Abhs 5.42 //

children.text: sarvākārāṃ viśuddhiṃ ye dharmāḥ prāptā nirāsravāḥ /
vāsanāyāḥ samuddhāto mahati karūṇā jane // Abhs_8.5 //
paripākaṃ gate hetau yasya yasya yadā yadā /
hitaṃ bhavati kartavyaṃ prathate tasya tasya saḥ // Abhs_8.9 //
varṣatyapi hi parjanye naiva bījaṃ prarohati /
akṣayatvācca tasyaiva nitya ityapi kathyate // Abhs_8.11 //
karau sapādau tarūṇau mṛdū ca mamutsadaiḥ saptabhirāśrayo 'sya // Abhs_8.13 //
ūūrṇāṅkitāsyo haripūrvakāyaḥ skandhau vṛtāvasya citāntarāṃsaḥ // Abhs_8.15 //
uṣīṣamūrdhā pṛthucārūjihvo brahmasvaraḥ siṃhahanuḥ suśuklāḥ // Abhs_8.16 //
nīlekśaṇe govṛṣapakṣmanetro dvātriṃśadetāni hi lakṣaṇāni // Abhs_8.17 //
saṃgrahāsevanaṃ dānaṃ praṇitasya ca vastunaḥ // Abhs_8.19 //
tāmrāḥ snigdhāśca tuṅgāśca nakhā aṅgulayo muneḥ /
mṛdvī tanvī ca raktā ca jihvā jimūtaghoṣatā /
cārūmañjasvaro daṃṣṭrā vṛttāstīkṣṇāḥ sitāḥ samāḥ // Abhs_8.28 //
śrīvatsaḥ svastikaṃ ceti buddhānuvyañjanaṃ matam // Abhs_8.32 //
karoti yena citrāṇi hitāni jagataḥ samam /
ā bhavātso 'nupacChinnaḥ kayo nairmāṇiko muneḥ // Abhs_8.33 //
gatīnāṃ śamanaṃ karma saṃgrahe ca caturvidhe // Abhs_8.34 //
saṃkete 'nupalambhe ca paripāke ca hehinām // Abhs_8.36 //
